purpose: Structured, bounded claim evidence and known unknowns for scientific review and downstream journalism. This is not a scientifically accepted release or legal determination.

CDFA Manchurian wild rice assessment and comments
Tu et al., Microbial Diversity in the Edible Gall

study_extraction.evidence_access: Publisher/PubMed abstract and bibliographic metadata checked; complete methods and sampling appendix not independently reviewed.
study_extraction.sampling_unit: Five harvested Zizania latifolia edible gall samples at differing growth/swelling stages; number of independent source farms or commerce lots not established from abstract.
study_extraction.method: Culture-based isolation of microorganisms from gall material; fungal colony identity by DNA sequencing, bacteria by MALDI-TOF, plus qPCR and ARISA microbial profiling.
study_extraction.directly_observed: Several Ustilago esculenta strains recovered in culture from sampled harvested edible gall material; qPCR DNA found across assessed stages.
study_extraction.not_measured: Not an infection challenge, experimental shipping/storage viability trial, retail consignment survey, fungal strain representativeness study, or North American native-host assay.
study_extraction.decision_relevance: Establishes recoverable fungal material at harvest in selected samples; cannot determine 2026 retail shipment infectivity.

sources.name: Chigira et al., Mating types of Ustilago esculenta in Japan

study_extraction.evidence_access: J-STAGE full HTML inspected on 2026-10-11: Methods—NARO Genebank strains; Results—Identification of mating types; Table 4 and Discussion. Abstract's compressed 'ten from Japan' description conflicts with actual Table 4 listing one from China.
study_extraction.sampling_unit: Two Japanese cultivated Zizania latifolia varieties (Shirakawa and Ittenkou) sampled in authors' paddies; a separate panel of ten NARO genebank Ustilago esculenta strains: nine sourced from Japan and one from China (yeast4, MAFF 305616), as itemized in Table 4.
study_extraction.method: Mating-type gene PCR and in-vitro mating/hyphal formation tests on selected fungal isolates; supplementary panel of ten NARO bank strains genotyped, with single Chinese-origin resource strain.
study_extraction.directly_observed: Mating-type assays and in-vitro mating among Japanese cultivars and archived accessions; 10 archived strains comprised nine Japan-origin and one Chinese-origin 'yeast4' (MAFF 305616), shown in Table 4. MAT-2/MAT-3 predominated in examined material; no native American host was assayed.
study_extraction.not_measured: No challenge test of American Zizania species, imported product, live edible material following US distribution, or a quantified native-rice infection probability.
study_extraction.decision_relevance: Demonstrates diversity of mating types and laboratory mating competence, not that any real imported retail stem initiates disease.
study_extraction.source_locator: Chigira et al. 2023 J-STAGE full HTML: Methods 'U. esculenta strains from the Genebank of the National Agriculture and Food Research Organization'; Table 4 (China yeast4 MAFF 305616).

study_extraction.evidence_access: Full open-access article abstract, Results (growth, mating, inoculation) and Discussion including mixed pairing outcome checked.
study_extraction.sampling_unit: Four selected fungal sporidial isolates: UeMT10/UeMT46 from edible white galls and UeT14/UeT55 from gray galls of Asian cultivar Longjiao 2; selected pairs are not a population prevalence sample.
study_extraction.method: In-vitro growth, germination and mating assays; inoculation on Zizania latifolia; microscopy and fungal genome resequencing.
study_extraction.directly_observed: MT/MT pairing under tested conditions showed impaired infection and growth; T types retained full cycle; certain tested T/MT cross pairings could mate and infect the Asian cultivar.
study_extraction.not_measured: No native American host was inoculated, no commercial shipment was sampled, no postharvest environmental dispersal was measured.
study_extraction.decision_relevance: Supports strain-specific infection differences and a crucial mixed-pair exception; no generic 'white gall equals safe' inference.

sources.source_section: Summary and Introduction: infected rhizome crop propagation versus wild host

study_extraction.evidence_access: Wiley full HTML text inspected on 2026-10-11, Results—Genome sequencing, assembly and annotation, Table 1; supplementary raw sequence files and computational pipeline not independently reproduced.
study_extraction.sampling_unit: One fungus-free wild Asian Zizania latifolia reference plant (accession HSD2, Taihu Lake region) whole-genome assembled; two cultivated Jiaobai accessions Zhejiao2 and Jiayou1 genome re-sequenced. These accessions are not biological replicate population samples of native North American rice.
study_extraction.method: Whole-genome shotgun assembly of wild HSD2 reference (83.4 Gb high-quality Illumina reads, ~140-fold coverage); genome resequencing of cultivated Zhejiao2 (24.0 Gb, 43.6x) and Jiayou1 (21.6 Gb, 39.1x); comparative genome and expression analysis.
study_extraction.directly_observed: Cultivated fungus-associated Z. latifolia showed differences in immune receptor and plant–pathogen interaction genes; edible-gall cultivars are maintained via infected rhizomes rather than flowering.
study_extraction.not_measured: No native North American Zizania examined; no fungal host-switch assay, imported edible-gall viability, shipping experiment, or representative estimate for all wild/cultivated plant populations.
study_extraction.decision_relevance: Distinguishes selected vegetatively maintained culinary crop from the living plant species capable of establishment as an invader.
study_extraction.source_locator: Guo et al. 2015 Wiley full HTML: Results section 'Genome sequencing, assembly and annotation', Table 1 comparing HSD2, Zhejiao2 and Jiayou1.

sources.name: Bowden and Eschen 1986, First Report of Wild Rice Diseases in Idaho
sources.source_section: Plant Disease 70:800, 1984 Idaho survey abstract, identified Entyloma lineatum stem smut, among other pathogens.

study_extraction.evidence_access: Original peer-reviewed Plant Disease disease note abstract read via APS 2026-10-11; complete methods/tables not independently obtained.
study_extraction.sampling_unit: Three Idaho commercial Zizania aquatica fields totaling 50 hectares and a 20-ha Benewah Lake location surveyed during anthesis and maturity in 1984.
study_extraction.method: Field plant-disease survey; fungi and bacteria isolated from stem and foliar lesions; smut identified by characteristic leaf/culm/sheath symptoms.
study_extraction.directly_observed: Smut diagnosed and reported as Entyloma lineatum along with named other pathogens at low incidence (<5%) and severity (<1%) in the examined 1984 sites.
study_extraction.not_measured: Not a species-specific Ustilago esculenta molecular screen, not a susceptibility challenge of North American native hosts, and not a broad absence survey of all future pathogen introductions.
study_extraction.decision_relevance: An original native wild-rice smut example is a different fungal taxon, so the word 'smut' alone cannot identify U. esculenta.

sources.name: Nyvall and Percich 1999, fungal brown spot and spot blotch in cultivated Minnesota wild rice
sources.source_section: Plant Disease 83:936–938; publisher/UMN abstract on disease source and lesion observations.

study_extraction.evidence_access: PubMed/University of Minnesota indexed abstract read 2026-10-11; full paper tables and raw lesion assays not independently reproduced.
study_extraction.sampling_unit: Cultivated Zizania palustris leaf/stem lesions sampled across development stages in Minnesota wild-rice fields; full field count and design not reconstructed from abstract.
study_extraction.method: Original field disease observations and fungal isolation from lesions, compared over plant growth stages.
study_extraction.directly_observed: Fungal brown spot attributed to Bipolaris oryzae and spot blotch to Bipolaris sorokiniana in Minnesota cultivated wild rice, with stage-specific lesion isolation results.
study_extraction.not_measured: Not Ustilago esculenta isolation, a contemporary native-bed disease census, or a host challenge for Asian jiaobai fungus.
study_extraction.decision_relevance: Provides a primary, positive native-wild-rice disease comparator rather than inferring native smut from unrelated Asian fungal biology.

sources.name: Zhao et al. 2019 Frontiers in Plant Science, origin of cultivated Zizania latifolia
sources.source_section: Materials and Methods: Plant Collection; Infected Plant Collection and Fungi Isolation; Results: Genetic Variations and wild/cultivar-like genotype distinction

study_extraction.evidence_access: Full original Frontiers HTML article and methods checked 2026-10-11; raw SSR genotype files, infection diagnosis materials and isolate vouchers not independently reassessed.
study_extraction.sampling_unit: 824 putative wild Asian Zizania latifolia accessions from 32 geographically sampled Chinese populations, 10-m plant separation, plus 135 cultivated landrace accessions; five field-observed infected wild accessions; 37 isolated fungal strains derived from 5 wild and 32 cultivated accessions.
study_extraction.method: Geographic plant sampling with foliar DNA, SSR plant genotyping; collection of visibly infected plants; fungal strain isolation and ITS-based comparison; population inference and cultivar-like genotype reassessment.
study_extraction.directly_observed: Five Ustilago esculenta-infected plants reported among the 824 putatively wild specimens from 32 populations; isolated U. esculenta from five infected wild accessions and 32 cultivated host accessions. Plant genotyping also revealed some putatively wild samples carried cultivar-like genotypes.
study_extraction.not_measured: No North American Zizania host tested, no experimental inoculation to prove other-host susceptibility, no US product sampling, no controlled transport-survival assay, and no unbiased national infection-prevalence estimate; 37 fungal isolates do not represent 37 wild host infection events.
study_extraction.decision_relevance: Provides direct observational evidence that fungus infection can occur in uncultivated Asian Z. latifolia; disproves categorical statements that infection is confined to edible cultivars, while preserving distinct wild Asian and native American hosts.

sources.name: Zou et al. 2024 Communications Biology, wild Zizania latifolia climate local adaptation and genomic offsets
sources.source_section: Abstract; Introduction references Zhao et al. 2019 for 5/824 wild infection; Methods and Results for separate 168-individual, 42-population Chinese wild Z. latifolia genomic survey

study_extraction.evidence_access: Full open-access Communications Biology text inspected 2026-10-11, including introduction, sampling methods and original wild population-genomic results; raw variant calls not reprocessed.
study_extraction.sampling_unit: 168 Chinese wild Zizania latifolia individuals collected in 42 populations, sampled 2–6 plants/population with >=10m separation; different sampling study from the Zhao 2019 824-accession host/fungus observation.
study_extraction.method: Whole-genome resequencing and population genetics; environment-associated SNPs, gene-selection and genotype–climate offset modeling across southern/northern Chinese wild lineages.
study_extraction.directly_observed: Two wild Z. latifolia genetic lineages, climate-related genomic differences and modelled offsets in Chinese populations; cites Zhao 2019 five-in-824 wild U. esculenta observation as prior work, without independently repeating that fungal survey.
study_extraction.not_measured: No novel U. esculenta-infected sample denominator or confirmation of native North American species; no US Great Lakes invasion forecast, import-law finding, or cross-host pathogenicity trial.
study_extraction.decision_relevance: Demonstrates wild Asian plant genetic and climatic diversity; prevents mistakenly treating a re-citation of Zhao 2019 as a second independent host-pathogen prevalence survey.

sources.name: Doan and Davis 2019 Mycology, Pythiogeton manoomin native Zizania palustris root/stalk rot
sources.source_section: Original open-access study Abstract, Materials/Methods: host range trials; Results: pathogenicity tests including re-isolation and ITS sequencing

study_extraction.evidence_access: Full open-access article snippets and PubMed original abstract accessed 2026-10-11; independent rerun of greenhouse inoculations and sequence comparison not conducted.
study_extraction.sampling_unit: California symptomatic wild-rice plants and controlled greenhouse inoculations on Zizania palustris cultivar Franklin plus other crop seedlings; inoculation test described as randomized block with ten replications and three repeat trials.
study_extraction.method: Isolate previously unknown Pythiogeton from diseased native rice; morphological and ITS phylogenetic identification; greenhouse pathogenicity challenge with mock-inoculated controls and recovery/re-isolation of organism from symptomatic plants.
study_extraction.directly_observed: Named oomycete Pythiogeton manoomin identified from wild rice; 84% of inoculated wild rice developed root/stalk rot in the study and 71% damping-off among tested seedlings; inoculation plus re-isolation supported causal diagnosis.
study_extraction.not_measured: No Ustilago esculenta diagnosis or inoculation, no cross-host test for Asian jiaobai fungus, no prevalence survey of naturally managed Great Lakes beds; 84% is an experimental result and not field population incidence.
study_extraction.decision_relevance: Positive methodological comparator for what a species- and host-resolved causal native-rice disease demonstration requires. Pythiogeton is an oomycete, not another name for Ustilago or Eballistra.

Does not establish environmental transmission from retailed food.

claims.statement: Tu et al. reported culturing several Ustilago esculenta strains from harvested Zizania latifolia galls.
limits: Culturing U. esculenta from gall tissue establishes recoverability at sampling, not infectious competence, spores at retail, or viability after shipping.
Five sampled galls at different swelling stages do not estimate the prevalence of viable fungus in the U.S. retail food supply.
claims.source_locator: Tu 2019 abstract: five harvested swollen-gall samples, isolates identified by DNA sequencing; not a post-shipment challenge

limits: Edible white tissue can contain fungal mycelium even without visible mature spore-bearing sori.
Strain-level infectivity and life-cycle differences matter; color is not a validated diagnostic test for a retail consignment.
claims.source_locator: Chigira 2023 introduction: M-T edible white galls with low sorus formation, T gray galls with abundant sori

Do not accuse stores based on this unresolved question.

claims.species: Zizania aquatica, Zizania palustris, Zizania texana
claims.scope: Modern North American native Zizania, no confirmed direct host record in reviewed set
claims.statement: The reviewed sources do not resolve modern native-host susceptibility or establish an actual native-bed infection.
limits: An uncertain host range is not proof of resistance or infection.
A secondary agency list is not a directly verified native diagnosis.
claims.source_locator: CDFA 2017 species list; CDFA 2018 botanist commentary; primary native host diagnosis missing from reviewed corpus

claims.species: Ustilago esculenta on cultivated Zizania latifolia
claims.scope: 2017 Chinese study of Longjiao 2 cultivar, two selected sexually compatible pairs of T and MT isolates, laboratory and greenhouse conditions
claims.statement: Zhang et al. (2017) observed T-type isolates from gray galls with more complete mating/infection and teliospore development than MT-type isolates from edible white galls; the tested MT isolates showed impaired infection and germination.
claims.source_locator: Zhang et al. 2017, PMC5719756, Abstract Results/Conclusion and infection assays; compare tested isolate pairs, not all field strains
limits: The assay tested specific isolates under laboratory/greenhouse conditions on Asian Z. latifolia; no American Zizania host was tested.
Impaired infection for MT isolates does not prove complete noninfectiousness of every edible gall or every strain during all possible exposures.
This study does not assay imported market products or occurrence in North American habitats.

claims.scope: USFWS April 2025 Ecological Risk Screening Summary, contiguous-US climate match and global invasion history
claims.statement: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service classified Zizania latifolia as High Risk based on demonstrated invasive history and broad contiguous-U.S. establishment climate match.
claims.source_locator: USFWS ERSS public summary, risk category, establishment climate matching and described history of invasiveness
limits: The high-risk screening result is a potential establishment risk, not a documented local manoomin-bed displacement or a state/federal prohibitory rule.
The conclusion concerns the introduced plant's ecological invasion risk; it does not establish U. esculenta host switching.

claims.scope: US retail edible stems from specified foreign origin, postharvest transport, disposal and exposure
claims.statement: Neither the presence of an infectious T-type strain nor the viability of a transmissible life stage after real food-distribution conditions has been established for the reported U.S. retail observations.
claims.source_locator: Contrast Zhang 2017 isolate-specific infection assays and Tu 2019 harvest isolation with missing shipment-specific retail sample and plant-health determination
limits: No conclusion of pathogen absence is justified by a missing commercial shipment assay.
No claim of infectious retail inoculum is justified by culturing an unrelated harvested gall.

claims.scope: 2017 controlled cross mating/inoculation study on Asian cultivar Longjiao 2
claims.statement: In Zhang et al. 2017, some T-type and MT-type fungal isolate combinations mated and produced successful infection in Asian Z. latifolia despite the tested MT/MT pair's infection defect.
claims.source_locator: Zhang et al. 2017 PMC5719756 Discussion, paragraph beginning 'Additionally, the sporidia from the T and MT strains could mate with each other'; Figures 5–6
limits: This is a cross among selected isolates in experimental conditions, not measured mixing or infection of actual market produce.
It invalidates an unconditional assumption that all MT-bearing material is unable to contribute to infection; it does not establish host compatibility with native American wild rice.

claims.scope: Comparison of fungus-maintained edible cultivars with wild or introduced populations of the same plant species
claims.statement: Artificially maintained edible jiaobai cultivars are propagated using infected rhizomes and lose flowering, while Z. latifolia as a plant species can reproduce and disperse via rhizomes and, in some settings, viable seeds.
claims.source_locator: Guo 2015 Summary/Introduction on crop selection; USFWS 2025 ERSS pp.2, 4–5 ecology; NZ MPI eradication webpage on seed and fragment spread
limits: Inferring that an edible cultivar typically fails to set seed does not establish all wild/introduced Z. latifolia are sterile.
The extent of seed-based establishment depends on locality and cultivar; no site-specific North American field estimate is supplied.

claims.scope: New Zealand Ministry for Primary Industries: National Interest Pest Responses programme and site management
claims.statement: New Zealand's biosecurity authority documents established Z. latifolia infestations and an active national eradication/containment programme, including an approximately 500-hectare Northland infestation area.
claims.source_locator: MPI 'Where manchurian wild rice has been found in NZ' and 'control and eradication' sections
limits: New Zealand's Biosecurity Act restrictions do not create corresponding U.S. import prohibitions.
Reported treatment duration and area are programme context, not a measured risk to any named American manoomin bed.

claims.scope: USFWS April 2025 risk summary quoting Terrell and Batra 1982 historical U.S. planting records
claims.statement: USFWS 2025 summarizes an older report of U.S. introduced living Z. latifolia plantings at federal research facilities and transfers to university researchers, separate from edible-stem retail reports.
claims.source_locator: Full ERSS first two PDF pages, Status in United States; 1982 Terrell and Batra passage quoted, including Patuxent and University of Minnesota research transfer
limits: These are historical plantings described in a 1982 account and repeated in a 2025 screening, not evidence those facilities still maintain them.
A living research planting is a distinct category from contemporary imported cut vegetable products.
USFWS separately labels MD and VA mapped records as non-established wild populations; do not turn 1982 research plantings into contemporary naturalization evidence.

claims.scope: Great Lakes Indian Fish and Wildlife Commission public Manoomin stewardship programme
claims.statement: GLIFWC describes a manoomin stewardship programme guided by Tribal rice chiefs, elders and member nations' natural-resource departments, connecting traditional ecological knowledge with scientific research on decline and habitat.
claims.source_locator: GLIFWC 'Ganawenindiwag Manoomin Anishinaabeg' public programme description, opening paragraphs and Habitat Requirements
limits: Public programme description does not constitute partnership or permission to disclose Traditional Ecological Knowledge and protected rice-bed locations.
Climate and water pollution pressures are active steward priorities, not evidence of U. esculenta presence.

claims.scope: Wisconsin DNR published 2026-10-07 Wild Rice Stewardship Council summit agenda
claims.statement: Wisconsin DNR published an October 7, 2026 council summit agenda with State/Tribal Technical Committee updates, review of priorities, and discussion of possible partners.
claims.source_locator: Wisconsin DNR 2026-09-10 event page: 2026-10-07 agenda items 1:30–2:45 p.m.
limits: An announced agenda does not verify that the summit occurred as planned or that any resolution or partnership was adopted.
No assumption of invitation or endorsement of 561 Group research is justified.

claims.scope: 2026 Fond du Lac Band, Minnesota Land Trust and DNR proposed Cedar Lake manoomin restoration
claims.statement: Minnesota DNR described a proposed project with the Fond du Lac Band and Minnesota Land Trust to restore water levels favorable to manoomin at Cedar Lake; the EAW public comment deadline was August 27, 2026.
claims.source_locator: Minnesota DNR 2026-07-28 press release, project description and comment deadline
limits: A proposal and past comment period are not proof the project was approved, funded, or completed.
Protected on-reservation restoration access is not permission for outside environmental observation or intervention.

claims.scope: Inspection of the enumerated federal noxious-weed taxa in 7 CFR 360.200 as of 2026-10-11
claims.statement: Zizania latifolia does not appear by name in the examined enumerated taxa of the federal noxious-weed list at 7 CFR 360.200.
claims.source_locator: 7 CFR 360.200, aquatic/wetland, parasitic and terrestrial weed lists; complete named-taxon search for 'Zizania' on 2026-10-11
limits: Absence from this named federal noxious-weed list is not an import approval, and other laws, import orders, or state rules can apply.
This is a legal-text observation, not a commodity-specific APHIS admissibility determination for China-origin jiaobai.

claims.scope: USFWS ERSS, 16 climate variables and Climate 6 match score for contiguous United States
claims.statement: USFWS identifies high climatic matches for Zizania latifolia in the Great Lakes Basin, among other contiguous U.S. regions; its continental Climate 6 score is 0.814, defined as the fraction of target points with score at least 6.
claims.source_locator: USFWS 2025 PDF text pp. 9–10, Section 7 Climate Matching: high-match regions and definition of Climate 6 score = count target points with score >=6 divided by all target points; 16 climatic variables.
limits: A climate-match fraction is not an 81.4% invasion probability, forecast of invasion, quantified risk to a particular manoomin bed, or direct species occurrence.
The USFWS High Risk assessment combines invasion history and climate match; weather suitability does not itself establish introduction or survival.

measurement.denominator: all FWS contiguous-US climate matching target points
measurement.regional_specificity: Great Lakes region named among areas with high match; 0.814 is a continental ratio, not a Great Lakes-specific probability
measurement.source_location: FWS ERSS section 7, Summary of Climate Matching Analysis

claims.scope: USFWS ERSS mapped GBIF-US 2023 occurrence records for Maryland and Virginia
claims.statement: USFWS states that mapped Maryland and Virginia records of Zizania latifolia do not represent established wild populations; they were excluded from the climate source-point calculation.
claims.source_locator: USFWS 2025 PDF text p. 9, Section 6 Distribution Within the United States, caption of Figure 2, MD/VA GBIF-US records not established wild populations.
limits: The excluded mapped records do not justify declaring naturalized Z. latifolia in Maryland or Virginia.
They also do not establish that introduced research plants are currently absent; they specify the evidentiary meaning of the mapped records as characterized by FWS.

claims.scope: Published North American wild-rice disease literature and recognized smut nomenclature
claims.statement: The smut reported on native wild rice as Entyloma lineatum is now treated taxonomically as Eballistra lineata, a different fungal species from Ustilago esculenta.
claims.source_locator: Bowden and Eschen 1986 Plant Disease 70:800 abstract (native Z. aquatica smut); McGilp et al. 2023 Crop Science §5.2 lists Eballistra lineata for northern Z. palustris; Species Fungorum record 467756 synonyms of Eballistra lineata.
limits: A symptom or the generic word smut does not identify Ustilago esculenta or establish a native host switch.
A 1984/1986 regional disease record is not a 2026 field screen or proof that future U. esculenta introductions cannot occur.

claims.scope: 1999 Minnesota wild-rice crop fungal brown spot and spot blotch study
claims.statement: Nyvall and Percich documented Bipolaris oryzae fungal brown spot and Bipolaris sorokiniana spot blotch in Minnesota cultivated northern wild rice.
claims.source_locator: Nyvall and Percich 1999 Plant Disease 83:936–938 indexed abstract; McGilp et al. 2023 Crop Science §5.2 reviewed fungal pathogens and their known impact.
limits: Positive evidence for these native-rice pathogens is not a Ustilago esculenta assay and not an estimate of manoomin disease across all natural waters.
Severity in commercial rice paddies cannot be transferred to Tribal-managed natural beds without conditions.

claims.scope: Peer-reviewed 2023 Crop Science review of northern wild-rice pathogens and crop management
claims.statement: The 2023 northern wild-rice review enumerates fungal brown spot, Eballistra lineata smut and several other established pathogens; it does not report a confirmed Ustilago esculenta infection of native wild rice among its listed diseases.
claims.source_locator: McGilp et al. 2023 Crop Science §5.2 'Fungal pathogens', crop disease list and cited literature; not a systematic absence screen of Ustilago.
limits: Absence of U. esculenta from a review's list is not evidence of resistance, negative molecular assays, or proof of no case anywhere.
The review focuses northern Z. palustris and production/stewardship science, not all North American species or wild-rice habitats.

claims.scope: China: Zhao et al. 2019, 824 putative wild host accessions from 32 populations; 5 reported infected plants
claims.statement: Zhao and colleagues (2019) observed five Ustilago esculenta-infected plants among 824 sampled putatively wild Asian Zizania latifolia accessions from 32 populations and isolated fungus from five wild accessions.
claims.source_locator: Zhao et al. 2019 Frontiers full text, Materials and Methods: Plant Collection (824/32) and Infected Plant Collection and Fungi Isolation (5 wild plants); Table 1 genotype caveats.
limits: Five observations in a geographically sampled set are not a national/time-invariant infection incidence, probability for all wild populations, or evidence that North American native Zizania are hosts.
Sampled wild accessions included plants later classified as cultivar-like based on genotype; archived isolates and botanical identities have not been independently rechecked.
Zou et al. 2024 cites this field observation but does not independently replicate its infected-plants count.

claims.scope: China: Zou et al. 2024, 168 wild plants from 42 populations and modelled future climate/genomic associations
claims.statement: Zou and colleagues (2024) used 168 wild Chinese Zizania latifolia from 42 populations to study plant population genomic adaptation to climate, citing but not repeating Zhao et al.'s earlier wild-host fungus sampling.
claims.source_locator: Zou et al. 2024 Communications Biology abstract, Introduction, Methods: Sample Collection and Results: Population structure; Zhao et al. 2019 original 824/32 infection sampling.
limits: This climate adaptation/genomics study does not quantify U. esculenta infection, forecast an invasion of American wetlands, or measure North American native host susceptibility.
The five-in-824 infection observation is attributed to Zhao 2019; citing it again is not an independent infected population sample.

claims.scope: Doan and Davis 2019 controlled greenhouse test of California symptomatic native wild-rice root/stalk rot
claims.statement: Doan and Davis (2019) isolated the oomycete Pythiogeton manoomin from symptomatic Zizania palustris, then documented disease following controlled inoculation with recovery of the organism from symptomatic plants.
claims.source_locator: Doan and Davis 2019 Mycology 10:243–249, Results—Pathogenicity tests; 84% rot and 71% damping-off in specified greenhouse inoculations, followed by re-isolation; ITS sequence analysis.
limits: The 84% and 71% are greenhouse treatment outcomes for Pythiogeton manoomin and are not field prevalence or cross-species U. esculenta results.
Pythiogeton is an oomycete and a separate organism from smut fungi Eballistra lineata and Ustilago esculenta.
These tests provide a methodological comparator, not independent evidence for the jiaobai pathogen infecting American manoomin.

release_gates.note: Do not derive a store-violation report, outbreak warning or accepted scientific release from this dataset without current primary receiving evidence and appropriate authority.

source_notes: Evidence statuses describe what source texts support in their own host/material context, not independent scientific acceptance, measured contemporary risk, or official U.S. commodity compliance. Sources may reference overlapping scientific study populations; event identifiers must not be treated as counts of independent infected plants. Added source-critical differentiators: partial MT infection phenotype is not a categorical safety rule because some T/MT mixed pairings infected cultivated Asian hosts; FWS 2025 documents old living-plant research introductions; NZ live-plant management differs from US food import status. Existing stewardship plans are public, not external consent.

extraction_protocol.description: Targeted source-critical extraction from four selected primary studies. Each row states access scope, actual sampling unit, tests, direct findings and absent measurements. Not a systematic literature screen, secondary independent peer-review receipt or an exhaustive risk appraisal. 2026-10-11 source audit additionally verified Guo Table 1 accession units, Chigira Table 4 archived strain origins, and USFWS Figure 2 and Climate 6 score interpretation. Added an original 1986 Idaho native-wild-rice smut survey and 1999 Minnesota primary brownspot study, plus 2023 northern wild-rice review and taxonomic synonymy to distinguish real native pathogens from U. esculenta.
extraction_protocol.inclusion: Original experiments or comparative genomics on Zizania latifolia–Ustilago esculenta biology relevant to edible tissue, strain behavior, mating or vegetative cultivation.
extraction_protocol.exclusion: Agency secondary host lists, historic specimen catalogues and regulatory webpages are kept as separate source kinds, not miscast as laboratory experiments.
extraction_protocol.reproducibility_limit: Candidate search histories, complete screening counts, all full methods, and original raw data have not been independently reanalysed. No PRISMA/ROSES compliance claim until those exist.
extraction_protocol.ethics: No experiments with live pathogens or plant material and no public disclosure of protected manoomin locations or traditional knowledge.
